summary: Beaverhead NF summit station by 1911, new frame building finished 1915, a cabin in the 1950s; listed gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Frame building with a sheet-iron roof and lightning rods (1915 newspaper item); a cabin on the summit in the 1950s (firelookout.com)
facts.status_note: Listed as Gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association and by firelookout.com; no source describes what remains on the summit

staffing.status: a forest guard rode to the summit in 1911; lookout men stationed on the peak in 1913 and 1915 (newspaper items); a ranger was hurt in 1915 and did not finish the season

events.note: Lookout station on Bald Mountain supported the riding patrol; a guard rode to the summit nearly every day (Big Hole Breezes, October 1911)
Dillon Tribune, August 1912: station 'just been established', one of the highest in the country; telephone line to the top
Orlando Connolly stationed on the peak; a windstorm tore his tent away (Dillon Tribune, August 1913)
New station building on the summit completed and covered with a sheet-iron roof, lightning rods fitted, after lightning caused rebuilding (Dillon Tribune, August 1915)
Arlie Connelly was stationed as lookout, was hurt again in August and could not resume work that season (Dillon Examiner, August 1915)
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: survey marker 30 feet southeast of a lookout building

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The earliest item, from October 1911, already describes a lookout station on the mountain; an August 1912 item says the station has 'just been established'. The story gives 1911 as the first mention and reports the 1912 wording. Neither item says when the first structure was built.

notes_for_editor: Every source for the 1911-1915 history is a newspaper item quoted on the Montana lookouts page, not the original paper; they were not checked directly. The firelookout.com entry is brief (one line of history). Two other Montana lookouts named Baldy Mountain must not be merged with this one: Sanders County, near Plains in the Lolo National Forest (FFLOS US 1608, MT 4; removed in 1990; record us-mt-baldy-mountain-2), and Lincoln County (NHLR US 1512, MT 90). Elevation is not set: newspapers give a little over 10,000 feet (1912), 10,050 feet (1913) and more than 9,000 feet (1915). No photo found. No correction to the record: kind 'ground' fits a frame building at ground level on the summit, and status 'gone' is supported by two sources.
